qs.q: A newborn infant presents with cyanosis and respiratory distress due to a congenital diaphragmatic hernia, most commonly through the posterolateral foramen. What is this foramen called?
qs.e: Herniation through the lumbocostal trigone or Bochdalek foramen represents the most frequent type of congenital diaphragmatic defect.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Anatomy Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: In a newborn with severe respiratory distress, which investigation is most useful to confirm a congenital diaphragmatic hernia?
o: Magnetic resonance imaging of the thorax
Chest radiograph of the lung fields
qs.e: Chest X‑ray readily shows bowel loops within the thoracic cavity, confirming diaphragmatic hernia. Echocardiography evaluates the heart, not the diaphragm.
qs.s: Neonatology 2: Prematurity and Respiratory Disorders: MCQs
